capability: Private parts stay sealed when a brief is reused
title: Private cards stay home.

hook.picture: Close on the whale copying last week's big brief card and changing only the name at the top; inside, a grey card from the old client is still there.

problem_in_viewer_words.body: I didn't mean to send the client's notes.
problem_in_viewer_words.who: consultant reusing last week's prompt for a new client

why_it_keeps_happening.picture: Pull back: a row of reused briefs, each made from the one before. Three more are copied, every 2 beats, then 1, then half; each still carries a grey card from someone else.
why_it_keeps_happening.words: Old briefs carry old secrets inside.

stakes.body: A client's private detail lands in someone else's work, and trust is gone for good.

solution_hint: Mark private notes. Check before they leave.

metaphor.body: A brief is a stack of cards on the line; a private card carries a sealed tab, and a send gate at the end of the line only opens for cards that belong to the client receiving the brief.

steps.picture: One card's tab fills violet with a small closed clasp: private to the old client.
The private card slides onto a short side branch of the line that belongs to that client only.
steps.words: Mark the private card. Seal it.

steps.picture: The reused brief rides the line toward a gate at the send point; ordinary cards pass through with a glow.
Push-in: the sealed card reaches the gate on a brief for the new client; the gate closes, rust, and holds it back.
steps.words: Sealed cards can't leave their client.

steps.picture: The brief goes on without it; the new client's pod reads and answers with a tick.
The side branch glows: one per client.
steps.words: Each client gets its own sealed scope.

real_case.claim: Context Atoms checks confidentiality before anything is sent; confidential scopes are sealed, and client work gets one child scope per client with Confidential ticked.

honest_limit.picture: The whale types the old client's name into the body of an ordinary card with a plain tab; it passes the gate with a glow and reaches the new pod.
honest_limit.words: Typed into a plain card, it slips through.

not_this.body: It checks labels, not what you typed.

ending_pattern.body: FELT framing: the whale copies last week's brief again and the other firm's pod swims in. The violet card stays behind at the closed gate; the pod reads, nothing is circled, its chip shows a tick.
ending_pattern.callback: The card that left with the pod in bar 3 now stays at the gate, in the same close framing.

end_belief.body: Mark what is private before you reuse it.

score_self.reason: Leaking a client note by reusing a prompt is felt by every consultant. The limit (typing into a plain card) is honest and pictured. Gate plus seal is two ideas; may crowd MOVE.
